# isDouble

<link-summary>Checks whether a value is a number with a fractional part.</link-summary>

<web-summary>isDouble() — Checks whether a value is a number with a fractional part. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>lang/number</code> · Since: 1.11.0</p>
</tldr>

```typescript
function isDouble(value: unknown): value is number;
```

A synonym of the `Float` family, offered under the name people reach for first. In JavaScript every number already is a double, so `double` names no runtime distinction of its own.

`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type      | Description         |
| :-------- | :-------- | :------------------ |
| `value`   | `unknown` | The value to check. |

## Returns

`boolean` — `true` when the value is a number with a fractional part; otherwise `false`.

In TypeScript the guard narrows `value` to `number` inside the branch.

## Examples

### What passes and what does not

```javascript
isDouble(1.5); // => true
isDouble(-0.1); // => true
isDouble(42); // => false
isDouble(1.0); // => false
isDouble(Infinity); // => false
isDouble("1.5"); // => false
```
